columns.description: Expense Description published for admin spend above £25,000 only

d010ad1b3aa96922fec0834183b8824882bd2c97.notes: Used the recorded row-0 header, which gives clean full column names. But sample_rows show, right after it, a month-label line ('Apr-12', mostly blank) and then a second, messier repeated header line ('Supplier Name\n', 'Amount ', 'Expenses Type \n' appearing twice, trailing newlines) before real data resumes at 'DFID, DFID, 11/04/2012...'. This looks like a file made by concatenating monthly export blocks, each carrying its own divider/header lines as literal rows. A naive header_row=0 read will pull in these divider and repeated-header rows as fake data throughout the file (this pattern likely repeats every month) — reviewer/build step must filter out embedded label and header-repeat rows before loading. 'description' is only populated for admin spend above £25,000, so it will be sparse/mostly empty. Review: April-September 2012 blocks map cleanly (11,472 rows); later blocks in the same file change header layout and are held (10,624 rows), reported on the page. A second mapping for those blocks is future work. Review: three block layouts in one file (Apr-Nov 'Supplier Name/Amount/Expenses…', then Dec onward reordered 'Date/Expense Type/Expense Area/Supplier/Transaction Number/Amount'); alt_columns covers them.

861e2c9c6d8bb61f42705e951014e843ddc72569.notes: 'Allocation Date' is the only date column available; mapped to payment_date but it may represent an allocation/posting date rather than the actual payment date — reviewer should confirm. Review: preview inspected; dates, suppliers and amounts read as published.

efcc2066e9e9bccd5a9090f2a29258f78438e51e.notes: 'amount' appears to be the net (pre-VAT) figure — sample rows show a separate 'vat' column at ~20% of 'amount' (e.g. amount 1960.0, vat 392.0). 'vat' and 'vat_code' are not mapped, per the rule against folding VAT into amount_gbp. 'beneficiary' is sometimes 'Redacted' in the sample rows; kept as published. Review: preview inspected; dates, suppliers and amounts read as published. Review 2026-09-07: body written as 'Leicester City Council' so the council's two datasets (2022 and current) sit under one name in the combined table.

constants.body: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

ffd3fc6de9870257e508be06f0df0e321d25bd2c.notes: Clean, single-header table; no issues noted. Review: preview inspected; dates, suppliers and amounts read as published.

46021c3a321f8028f71c5fec241aa007db9218e9.notes: Table also carries 'Organisational unit' (a directorate-level field, e.g. 'People Directorate') and 'Expenditure category' (a broader category than 'Detailed Expenses type', e.g. 'Supplies and Services') — only one column each is allowed for expense_area/expense_type, so these two were left unmapped; reviewer should check whether they'd be preferred over 'Service label'/'Detailed Expenses type'. 'Capital/\nRevenue' and 'Supplier ID' also unmapped, no schema slot for them. Review: preview inspected; dates, suppliers and amounts read as published.

1290aae1e6a8cbfa60bc8d47c56780709231061e.reject: Every sample row has 'Supplier Name' populated as 'BARCLAYCARD PROCUREMENT CARD' with the same 'Voucher' number, split across many small (including negative) amounts by expense type/area — this is a procurement-card (GPC) statement broken out by spend category, not supplier-level payment lines.

fd8703927e1188f4c68987c641e496ca9df08f85.notes: Minimal 3-column table (Supplier, Payment Date, Amount only); no expense_area/expense_type/reference/description/period available. Review: preview inspected; dates, suppliers and amounts read as published. Layouts: 2 added: main 'Supplier/Payment Date/Amount' layout (12 files) already covered by existing columns; underscored 'Supplier/Payment_Date/Amount' layout (2 files, Oct-2011) added.

f7364e529c276bf35e6c9b19cda7baba4f8448fd.notes: Minimal 3-column table (Supplier, Payment Date, Amount only), same shape as the other Greenwich source in this family; no expense_area/expense_type/reference/description/period available. Review: preview inspected; dates, suppliers and amounts read as published. Layouts: 4 added: 'Supplier/Payment Date/Amount' layout (10 files) already covered; 'Supplier/Amount/Payment Date' reordered layout (18 files) already covered by the same column names; 'Creditor Name/Invoice Line Amount/Payment Date/LA Department/Expenditure Category' layout (10 files, mid-2014) added; underscored 'Creditor_Name /Invoice Line Amount/Payment_Date' variant of that layout (2 files, early 2015) added.

adf25f9f31269c417f96ee00c75c837896bdbbdb.notes: File starts with a title line ('Wales Office spend over £500', 'May-10' ...) at row 0, a blank row at row 1, then the real header (ENTITY, EXPENSE_AREA, PAYMENT_DATE, PAYMENT_NUMBER, SUPPLIER_NAME, INVOICE_AMOUNT, NAC_DESCRIPTION, Service provided) at row 2 — header_row set to 2 accordingly. Reviewer should confirm the blank-row count is consistent for other months' files in this same series if more get added later. Review: 17 of 23 rows have no date in the source; kept with payment_date null. Layouts: 8 added: Oct-2012 'Payment Date/Supplier Name/ Amount /NAC Description/Service Supplied' layout added; Sep-2012 'Date/Supplier/Amount/Payment No/Service Description' layout added; Aug-2012 'PAYMENT DATE/SUPPLIER NAME/INVOICE AMOUNT/EXPENSE_AREA_1' layout added, also covering the same-shaped Jul-2012 layout (extra PO/invoice-value columns) and the Jun-2012 layout (16 files); Feb-2011 underscored 'PAYMENT_DATE/SUPPLIER_NAME/INVOICE_AMOUNT' layout (2 files) added separately since its description column reads 'SERVICE SUPPLIED' rather than 'Service provided'; Dec-2010 11-column layout added, using 'EXPENSE_TYPE_6' over the sibling 'EXPENSE_TYPE_3'/'NAC_LEVEL_6' fields for expense_type (reviewer should check which is preferred); Nov-2010 title-row file (real header two rows down, per the brief's title-row rule) added with its own single 'EXPENSE_TYPE' column. Review 2026-09-06: the June and July 2011 files carry amounts formatted with a dollar sign ('$1,145.00'), a spreadsheet formatting artefact; the figure is read as pounds, which is what the return states.

096c8c488b60488acea2a888e215be9ea43aff19.notes: File starts with a title line ('Payments for Publishing for Invoices paid between 01-SEP-2022 and 30-SEP-2022') at row 0, real header at row 1 — header_row set to 1 accordingly. Note the exact header text for payment_date and expense_area carries a leading space (' Paid Date', ' Department') in the source. 'Cost Centre' holds a code (e.g. 'D2510'), not a text description, but it is the only expense-type-like field available; reviewer should sanity-check this choice. 'Irrecoverable VAT' is present but not mapped to amount_gbp, per the rule against folding VAT into the payment amount. Review: expense_type is the council's cost-centre code, as published. Review 2026-09-06: the November 2023 and May 2024 returns use 'Payment Number', 'Line Amount' and 'Subjective Desc' (second layout). The December 2025 return's header lists a Paid Date column but its rows do not carry one, so every value sits one column left of its label; the third layout reads that file by its contents and those rows have no payment date.

3ef6586edd03fb6c63b21861f171ee3ec7a681d4.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the title ('Spend over £500 in Government Equalities Office'). Small file (16 rows in sample count), clean single header. constants.body: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

cad03d565abbb431d95bde21a877f6716a06d94b.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the title ('Spend over £500 in the Government Offices for the Regions'). Same column shape and same publisher string as the DCLG source already mapped in this file (job d010... no, job ffd3fc6d...); body taken from this source entry's own 'publisher' field, which is the modern successor department, not 'Government Offices for the Regions' itself. Clean single header, no issues. Review: Government Offices for the Regions return, published under the successor department's name.

45e5c4b154f37f9657e1533c3cea960c4d928d92.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the title ('Expenditure over £500'). Only 'invoice_date' is available — there is no separate payment-date column, so payment_date is mapped to invoice date; reviewer should confirm this is acceptable given the schema's stated preference for payment over invoice date. Column is named 'net_amount' but no VAT column appears anywhere in this table's header, so it is mapped as the published amount as-is (not adjusted); reviewer should double check whether 'net' implies VAT was stripped out elsewhere. Many sample suppliers are '*Redact - Personal Information' — kept as published (redaction is the publisher's own text, not something applied here). Negative amounts (credits) appear in samples and are kept with sign preserved. Review: only an invoice date exists; payment_date carries it. net_amount as published, no VAT column.

constants.body: UK Commission for Employment and Skills

e26bf628169d3aecf4e1052362a421c16a630da8.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the title ('Spend over £500 in the UK Commission for Employment and Skills'). 'Date' includes a literal time component in the sample ('10/01/2014 00:00') — always midnight in samples shown, so date extraction should be safe, but reviewer should confirm. No expense_area-equivalent column exists (only department-level 'Department Family'/'Entity'), so left unmapped. Table also carries 'Year' and 'Period' columns, but sample values ('C', '12') don't read as a clean, publishable period label, so 'period' was left unmapped — reviewer should check what these encode before adding. 'Supplier' values carry an embedded supplier code prefix (e.g. 'ASP002 - Aspero Limited') — kept exactly as published, not split apart. Not mapped, no schema slot: Supplier postcode, Supplier type, HOME_CREDIT, HOME_DEBIT, Contract Number, Project Code, Expenditure type. Review: no dates or expense area in the source; Year/Period columns opaque and left unmapped. Layouts: 7 added: Oct-2011 'Pay Period/Pay Date/Pay Value/Supplier' layout (7 files) has an apparently mislabeled header — the sample data shows the 'Pay Period' column holding the payment date and the 'Pay Date' column holding the numeric amount, with 'Pay Value' a constant 'PAY' marker; mapped by data position rather than label, reviewer should double-check; Nov-2011 same-shape layout (5 files) covered by that same mapping; Jan-2014 detailed BIS layout already covered by the existing columns; Apr-Dec-2013 detailed BIS layout (space-padded ' Amount ', 4 files) already covered; Nov-2012 layout (1 file) with correctly labelled 'Pay Date'/'Pay Value' columns added; one 2013 BIS layout (1 file) using 'Transaction Number' in place of 'tran_ref' added; skipped one 'Supplier'/'Gross Value' totals-only layout (64 rows, per-supplier totals not per-payment lines). Review 2026-09-06: the 2011-12 monthly files carry mislabelled headers: the date sits under 'Pay Period', the amount under 'Pay Date' and a literal 'PAY' under 'Pay Value' (sample row ' 20-Oct-11', '527.11', 'PAY', supplier); the second alternate layout maps them by content. The May 2012 file has only Supplier and Gross Value, so those 64 rows carry no date or period.

cf8fc911f167104ad7bf020b78493813d2ad0eb8.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the title ('Administrative spend over £500 in UK Trade and Investment'); note the title scopes this file to administrative spend only, not the department's full spend-over-£500 return — reviewer should check whether a separate 'programme spend' file exists for the same body/period that would need its own mapping. 'Description' is empty in every sample row, likely sparse throughout. Sample suppliers include 'Personal Expense, Name Witheld' (employee expense claims) — kept as published per the rule on personal names published under the transparency code. Review: administrative spend only; lines below £500 kept as published.

ad249d35bc190e882a9a4faa7fbb81a139ae86f4.notes: Single layout across both files (unique_id, payment_date, department, beneficiary, purpose_of_expenditure, amount, vat, vat_code, merchant_category). 'vat' and 'vat_code' are present but not mapped: the family rule keeps VAT separate from amount_gbp and there is no dedicated VAT schema column, so both are left out (amount samples read e.g. '1010.0' with vat '0.0', consistent with 'amount' already being net/gross as published). 'merchant_category' (e.g. 'Legal Fees & Charges', 'Home Care') is used for expense_type as the closest categorical field; 'department' (e.g. 'Adults', 'City Developments and Neighbourhood') is used for expense_area. Review 2026-09-07: body written as 'Leicester City Council' so the council's two datasets (2022 and current) sit under one name in the combined table. Review 2026-09-07: 159,670 lines May-December 2022 across two files; merchant_category stands in for expense_type as the only categorical column.

c9177a5a76909e19b03b336a53a1627b643be0b1.notes: The brief lists 8 layout entries for the 60 files, but only 2 distinct header-naming schemes among them; the other 6 are the same two schemes with a varying number of extra, empty-header trailing columns (column_count 19/21/29/30/40 vs 7), evidently trailing commas in some quarterly exports rather than real extra fields — none of them carry any header text, so nothing is lost by leaving them unmapped. 'columns' covers the 'Service Area'/'Expense Type'/'Invoice Payment Date' naming (45 files: the 36-file primary layout plus the three same-named padded layouts, 3+3+3 files); 'alt_columns' covers the 'Service Label'/'Expense Category'/'Date' naming (15 files: 11 plus the three same-named padded layouts, 2+1+1 files). 'Body Name' is always literally 'TfGM' in the sample rows and is not mapped; constants.body uses the brief's full publisher name instead, matching the convention in the other reviewed entries. No description/period source column is available in either layout. Review 2026-09-07: 60 quarterly files, April 2011 to March 2026, two header schemes. Credits are published in accounting brackets, '(2,586.20)', and are read as negative amounts; five rows with a blank amount are held.

486018dd852f32dded2fa96788e960b215d0c74c.notes: Two layouts in the brief differ only by three trailing columns present in one (ObjectId, _lon, _lat) and absent in the other; every column used here has identical header text in both, so no alt_columns entry is needed. 'Date_Paid' and 'Date_Received' are both blank in every sampled row — payment_date will likely be null for most/all rows; kept as the semantically closer field to 'payment_date' (schema payment_date is not required). 'Customer_Supplier_Description' holds the actual supplier/contractor name (e.g. 'Urbaser Ltd', 'Tivoli Group Limited') despite its generic-sounding header, and is mapped to supplier. 'Service_Label' (e.g. 'Environmental and regulatory services', 'Planning Services') is used for expense_area over the more granular 'Division_Description' (e.g. 'Client Services (Depot)', 'Planning'); reviewer should check which is the better fit. 'Capital_Revenue' (Revenue/Capital flag) and the various *_Code/ObjectId/_lon/_lat columns have no matching schema column and are left unmapped. Title states 'Spend Over 250', so threshold_gbp is 250, not the family default of 500. Review 2026-09-07: Date_Paid and Date_Received are blank in every row, so payment_date is null and the period is taken from the title (financial year 2024 to 2025). The layer was fetched in three formats; one is kept.
